events.text: Trump posts that a call with Putin produced a Russian diesel supply deal
Musk reportedly says Zelensky "has gone too far", replying to a Trump video. Not captured here; reported only
Trump announces an "ENERGY CEASEFIRE", saying "Both parties have agreed"
Ukrainian terminals start dropping above about 160 km/h, some lower. Reuters puts the restriction on 13 and 14 October
Beskrestnov, Zelensky's technology adviser: "Our defense forces were not notified in advance ... this cannot be a coincidence"
Fedorov: Starlink up to 160 km/h "is being restored"; "Removing Starshield's speed limit entirely is now critical"; thanks Musk
Musk: "Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government. Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS."
Musk: "True", quoting a post that says Starshield is under US government control
Reuters: Pentagon officials were told by the White House to slow Starshield. A senior US official: "No such request was ever made by the president"
Tillis asks the DoD Inspector General to investigate. Bacon and Blumenthal criticise
Telegraph: Musk proposed the cap to Trump, and Trump agreed
Zelensky: a road test in EU countries held the link above 180 km/h, so the limit applies only in Ukraine. He calls it "a planned operation"
Rubio: "it wasn't deliberate. We have nothing to do with that"; Ukraine has no Starshield access "at this moment"; reports of White House involvement "categorically false"
Zelensky on NBC: "a message from the American government to limit this speed, and technically SpaceX did it"
Trump on Russia sanctions: "Zelenskyy is using Diesel Refineries in Russia as a target"
Trump thanks "our legendary friend, Elon Musk" for giving SpaceX stock through Trump Accounts
Hegseth: "We haven't pulled anything back ... that's where Starlink has the option to make those decisions"
POLITICO: Democrats plan probes of Musk, including "his possible role last week in throttling" Ukraine's access
WSJ: Musk ordered the slowdown. Published minutes after SpaceX's quarterly earnings, and not raised on the earnings call
Musk: "Some fools still think the legacy news is real. Amazing." A WSJ reporter asks if that is his comment on the story. No answer was found
Trump calls Musk and asks him to lift the restriction (WSJ, per S17 and S18)
Trump: "Whether I called or whether somebody else called, doesn't make any difference ... The bottom line, he put it back."
A Ukrainian official: "Overall, nothing has changed anywhere"; the 161 km/h cap remains
Rubio: "that is governed by a private commercial contract", including "what speeds they'll allow it to be used at"
SpaceX files its 10-Q. It says nothing about Ukraine or Russia
Blumenthal opens an inquiry, with letters to Musk and Hegseth
